title: Tawantinsuyu and the Qhapaq Ñan: The Se Passive

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the passive with *se* from B1 Unit 6: *se* + a verb in the third person, which agrees with the thing that receives the action (*Se venden casas*). It is the usual way to say what is built, used or recorded without naming who did it, which suits the history of an empire.

sections.title: At work on the topic
rows: Se construyeron puentes colgantes de fibra vegetal.
Se usaba el quipu para anotar números.
En 2014 se inscribió el Qhapaq Ñan en la lista de la UNESCO.
a one-off event in the past
Se guardaban alimentos en depósitos del Estado.
a habit in the past: imperfect

items.spanish: En el Qhapaq Ñan se construyeron escaleras y puentes en las montañas.
items.english: Stairs and bridges were built in the mountains along the Qhapaq Ñan.

items.spanish: En el imperio inca se usaban quipus para anotar números.
items.english: In the Inca empire quipus were used to record numbers.

items.spanish: En 2014 se inscribió el Qhapaq Ñan en la lista de la UNESCO.
items.english: In 2014 the Qhapaq Ñan was added to the UNESCO list.

items.spanish: Se guardaban alimentos en depósitos del Estado.
items.english: Food was stored in state storehouses.

sections.content: The verb agrees with the thing, not with *se*: *se usaban quipus*, not *se usaba quipus*. If you want to name the doer, switch to the *ser* passive: *fue construido por los incas*.
